_comment: Provenance and licence review for third-party dish data.
STATUS: nothing here is imported. The two best-matching datasets were licence-checked
on 2026-10-06 and both were refused. See `verdicts` below for the evidence. The
classification in scripts/classify-recipe-roles.mjs therefore remains hand-authored from
each pack's own category taxonomy, which is the more reliable source for the launch
Any future import must go through scripts/import-world-dishes.mjs, which refuses to
write anything until every licence claim about a dataset is known and permissive. The

verdicts.dataQuality: excellent fit — 765 dishes, only 1 mentioning Nepal

columnMapping.note: type_of_dish and time_of_day map cleanly onto our vocabulary. Implemented and tested in scripts/import-world-dishes.mjs, ready if the licence is ever cleared.

time_of_day.anytime, other: no restriction, expressed as an empty list

licenseClaims.note: Prose. Terms add that it is 'primarily intended for evaluating foundation models', permits 'careful fine-tuning', and prohibits using it to build 'prompt templates for the generation of training data'.
Machine-readable metadata distributed with the dataset.

blockingReason: The two official statements conflict, and the more restrictive one governs.
cc-by-nc-sa-4.0 is non-commercial, so it cannot be used in a product distributed
through the App Store and Play Store. Its share-alike term would also attach to
derived packs. We did not choose the permissive reading of LICENCE.md, because
picking the more convenient of two conflicting licence claims is exactly the mistake
additionalConstraints: Linked images carry their own per-row licences and some are known non-commercial; the authors also prohibit using the images for model training. Image columns are therefore dropped unconditionally by the importer.
Contributors consented to their photographs specifically, which is a narrower permission than a blanket dataset licence.
verdicts.toClear: Ask the maintainers which licence governs, and whether they will relicense the data (not the images) as CC-BY-4.0. Cite the conflict between LICENCE.md and the Croissant metadata.

verdicts.dataQuality: good taxonomy, but no dish role or meal time

licenseClaims.note: No license tag and no license field in cardData. Verified via https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/worldcuisines/food-kb.

blockingReason: No licence is declared, so nothing establishes permission to use it. An absent
licence is all rights reserved, not an implied open licence.
Separately, it carries no per-dish role or meal time, so it would not have solved
the problem we were solving even if it were licensed.
dataHygieneNote: The `alias` column contains respondent free-text that leaked into the data — the
'Arroz con maiz' row carries placeholder respondent fields including name, age and
city. Any use would need those rows stripped before the data went anywhere.
verdicts.toClear: Ask the publisher to publish a licence. Do not import rows in the meantime.

summary: Found while auditing the Family Nutrition screen: the app cannot currently compute
nutrition for the food it plans. This is the largest data gap, and the one that most
Three problems, only the third of which is fundamentally a data problem.

detail: apps/mobile/lib/consumption/family_nutrition_screen.dart scores every logged meal
with referenceDalBhatBatch, a single hard-coded dal-bhat batch. The code comment
admits this ('used until per-recipe batch composition is logged'), but the effect is
that a household logging thukpa or momo is shown dal bhat's kcal, protein, fibre,
carbs and fat. Every number on that dashboard is dal bhat's unless the meal was
dal bhat.
Masked by problem 2: the lookups mostly failed anyway, so the totals were not
obviously wrong to the eye.
recommended: Until real composition exists, either stop scoring meals that are not dal bhat, or
label the values as dal-bhat reference figures rather than the household's intake.
A confident number that is not the user's food is worse than an acknowledged gap.
Then derive a batch per recipe from that recipe's own ingredients.

detail: Region packs write ingredient ids in snake_case (mustard_oil, wheat_flour, kalo_dal)
while NutritionEngine.compositionTable writes kebab-case (mustard-oil, wheat-flour,
black-lentil). compositionFor matched on exact id and returned null otherwise, so the
ingredient silently contributed zero nutrients. No error, no coverage report, so
nothing looked wrong.
Measured across all four packs: 66 of 672 ingredient references resolved to nutrient
data, 10%. Mustard oil appears 101 times and resolved to nothing.
Fixed by folding case and the separator, plus an alias table for names that genuinely
differ (kalo_dal -> black-lentil, palungo -> spinach, ghiu -> ghee). Coverage becomes
yieldFor had the same defect and failed more quietly: an unmatched factor became 1.0,
a plausible no-op rather than an obvious failure, so cooked weights were wrong without
anything looking wrong.
84 distinct ingredients used by the packs still have no nutrient data. By usage:
garlic 62, ginger 35, ghee 32, tomato 32, onion 27, turmeric 23, green_chili 20,
timur 16, fenugreek_seeds 14, red_chili 13, cardamom 11, cumin 9, goat_meat 9,
sesame 9.
Most are aromatics used in tens of grams. They matter for flavour and for any future
micronutrient work but contribute little to kcal or protein, so the sensible order is
staples and protein sources first (rice, dal, flour, meat, ghee), then vegetables,
then aromatics.

recommendedSource.license: public domain (US Government work); clears scripts/lib/dataset-license-gate.mjs
why: Authoritative per-100 g values including the micronutrients this dashboard would
eventually want, which no regional table here covers to the same depth.
Machine-readable API and bulk downloads, so the import is scriptable.
Public domain: no attribution obligation and no non-commercial conflict, unlike
every candidate in the verdicts section above.
caveats: USDA describes foods generically and in Western preparation. Entry selection has to
be done per ingredient by hand; automatic name matching will pull the wrong thing
for ingredients such as timur (citron) or jimbu (dried fern) that USDA may not carry.
Values must be recorded per 100 g raw to match compositionTable, and should keep the
CompositionSource marker so USDA-sourced rows stay distinguishable from IFCT ones.
